key_insight: Shape-informed hemodynamic surrogates benefit most from active learning and physical consistency during fine-tuning, while generalization is limited primarily by geometric coverage.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable prediction of patient-specific aortic velocity and pressure fields toward real-time cardiovascular flow assessment.
method: Generate synthetic aortic CFD solutions with automatically adjusted, physiologically consistent boundary conditions.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields from a common reference and train Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net surrogates.
Evaluate active learning and differentiable finite element residual constraints for data-efficient training and fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Peak-systolic predictions and out-of-distribution studies show fine-tuning gains from gradient- and subspace-based acquisition and physical consistency, but the abstract reports no numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Predictions for anatomies outside the geometric parametrization's support may remain unreliable regardless of network architecture.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
